objections.reason: Same instruction leak in Portuguese: "... na forma de dicionário: 忙しい様です ('parece estar ocupada'). Rewrite: 'ようです aqui expressa aparência/conjectura baseada em evidência; ...', com sentido de aparência/conjectura." An English editorial command ('Rewrite:') inside pt-BR learner prose, plus the same orphaned trailing clause. (2) 'Quanto a (eu)' is ungrammatical pt-BR: after 'quanto a' the pronoun must be oblique ('quanto a mim'), never the nominative 'eu'. lit_en has the same false topic ('As for (me), I want to become a wealthy person').

It also contradicts the record's own after fields: expl_en/expl_pt still say "There are two short sentences" / "São duas frases curtas", and both translations are two sentences ("I got tired. The kana is still こーひー, so romaji no longer mirrors kana, and sent:gen-d3f700a0e433 in this very batch keeps 'ko-hi-oatatakakushitemoraemasuka' untouched — after this patch the same katakana word is romanized two different ways inside one batch. objections.reason: COLLATERAL DAMAGE: the number fix was correct (juusan / sanjuu) but 言った, which was correctly romanized 'tteitta' in before, was corrupted to 'tteixtsuta' — an IME keystroke encoding of っ that is not romaji and does not mirror the kana じゅうさんっていった.
objections.suggested: juusantteitta?soretomosanjuu?

objections.reason: LAYER A: this is a gen=false Tatoeba record and 'before' has no texts.translation.en at all; the patch creates one with AI-authored English ('Looks like the lonely days will continue for a while, huh.'). The op claims to be correcting a source English it quotes ('Oh well, recently I continue...'), but that string is absent from the before snapshot, so the diff cannot be verified as fixing the described defect and instead writes new AI prose into the authoritative English slot of a Layer A record. Either the diff is built against the wrong baseline or the Tatoeba-linked en is being silently rewritten.

The new pt-BR role carries the QA justification into the learner-facing label: "adjetivo de inexistência (predicado) — mesma etiqueta usada em お金が全然ないの". A cross-record consistency argument is corpus-build metadata, not a role label. It also uses an em dash, and role.en was left as 'negation auxiliary' — the exact wording the op declared wrong — so en and pt-BR now disagree.
objections.suggested: adjetivo de inexistência (predicado)

objections.reason: The op's defect (気 mislabelled as an object when it is the subject of existential ある with が omitted) was fixed only in pt-BR. role.en still says 'object (the desire to speak)', so the same token is now labelled 'object' in English and 'sujeito de ある' in Portuguese. The defect the op describes still ships in half the record.
objections.suggested: subject of ある (particle が omitted)

objections.reason: Same half-application: ない was relabelled 'predicado de negação de existência' in pt-BR but role.en still reads 'negation auxiliary (second option)' — the wording the op identified as wrong. en and pt-BR now describe the token differently.
objections.suggested: existential-negative predicate (second option)

objections.reason: The correction was spliced in without removing the old tail, producing ungrammatical, self-contradicting prose: "たとえようもない = 'there is not even a way to compare' + も + ない means 'there is no way even to compare', i.e. 'incomparable'." The whole expression is first equated to its meaning and then re-decomposed as that meaning '+ も + ない'. The identical splice error is in structure_explanation.pt-BR ("たとえようもない = 'não há nem um modo de comparar' + も + ない significa...").
objections.suggested: ...a set expression where たとえよう is the masu-stem たとえ + the noun よう (様, 'way'); よう + も + ない = 'there is not even a way to compare', i.e. 'incomparable'.

objections.reason: lit_en was rewritten to 'rarely goes out' but lit_pt was left as 'Quanto a ela, raramente não sai.' In Portuguese that reads as 'she rarely does NOT go out' — the opposite of めったに外出しない, and exactly the double-negative inversion this same batch flags as major and fixes in sent:tatoeba-95287 ('raramente não existe' -> 'raramente existe'). After the patch the two literal translations of one sentence assert opposite meanings.
objections.suggested: Quanto a ela, raramente sai (lit. raramente + não-sai).

objections.reason: Only pt-BR was cleaned. structure_explanation.en still ends with 'The focus is coverage of an alternative question' — the same corpus-build 'coverage' jargon the op ordered removed — and still opens with the dangling cross-record reference 'Same idea as the previous sentence', which this batch treats as a defect in sent:tatoeba-91408. The record's own violations array flags this exact en string as I5_METADATA_LEAK and the patch leaves it untouched.
objections.suggested: The choice between alternatives is made only by juxtaposing two separate questions divided by a comma (、), without それとも. ... The focus is the alternative-question pattern ('A ですか、B ですか').

objections.reason: The record carries live I5_METADATA_LEAK violations on both structure_explanation.en and .pt-BR, and the patch changes neither: pt-BR still says 'O alvo é cobertura N4' and en still says 'The target is N4 coverage'. This is exactly the leak that sent:tatoeba-92348 in this same batch removes, so the batch ships the same defect fixed in one record and unfixed in another.
objections.suggested: ...'não é que / não significa que'. O ponto-chave é わけではない suavizando a negação ('não exatamente').

objections.reason: The actual defect the op describes was never applied: tokens still contain the null-glossed fragments 何 (tokens[0], r=なん) and 歳 (tokens[1], r=さい) alongside the combined 何歳 (tokens[2], r=なんさい), so concatenated token surfaces read 何歳何歳で… and no longer tile the sentence 何歳で自転車に乗れるようになった. Only a role string was edited.

The op's fix was never applied: tokens[6] (the second て of 待ってて, the contracted いて auxiliary) still has gloss/role/note all null, while tokens[5] still carries gloss 'to be (progressive auxiliary, contracted)' and the note '待ってて = contraction of 待っていて'. The annotation was not moved; only a pt-BR role string was replaced with an instruction.

The op explicitly says to remove the leaked QA meta-commentary 'from both language versions', but note.en still reads "imperative form of くれる; the gloss 'to get dark' is noise" — an internal QA remark about a stale dictionary gloss, shipped to learners.
objections.suggested: imperative form of くれる

objections.reason: The field was edited but still applies the 'Quanto a X' topic device to 子供を, which is marked by を, not は: 'Aquele que é pai ou mãe, quanto aos filhos, deve criá-los firmemente é.' The as-for device must mirror は only. The sentence's actual topic (親たる者は) is rendered without it, so the device is attached to the wrong particle.
objections.suggested: Quanto àquele que é pai ou mãe, os filhos com firmeza criar deve é.

objections.reason: Collateral damage while fixing the さんぷんかん counter: `before` had the correct "sanfunkandakematteyaru." body, `after` is "sanpunkandakemaxtsuteyaru。". The counter fix (sanpun) is right, but 待って was re-romanized as "maxtsute" — the sokuon っ was emitted as the literal IME escape "xtsu" — and the ASCII sentence period was replaced by a full-width 。. Romaji no longer mirrors the kana まって and no longer matches the punctuation convention used by every other romaji in the batch.
objections.suggested: sanpunkandakematteyaru.

objections.reason: Same corruption pattern while fixing 止め→やめ: `after` is "wakaxtsuteinaifuriosurunowayamenasai。". The やめなさい fix is correct, but 解って came out as "wakaxtsute" instead of "wakatte" (sokuon emitted as the IME escape "xtsu"), and the terminal "." became a full-width 。. The romaji contradicts the kana わかっていない.
objections.suggested: wakatteinaifuriosurunowayamenasai.

objections.reason: The editing instruction was pasted into the learner-facing field instead of being executed. `after` ends: "...reinforced by the adverb いつも ('always'). Delete this sentence; end after \"…reinforced by the adverb いつも ('always').\"" This is worse than the leak the op was fixing — the corpus would now ship an editorial directive to learners.
objections.suggested: ...to indicate a habitual/ongoing situation, reinforced by the adverb いつも ('always').

objections.reason: Same failure in pt-BR: `after` ends with "...reforçada pelo advérbio いつも ('sempre'). Remover a frase; terminar após \"…reforçada pelo advérbio いつも ('sempre').\"" The QA instruction replaced the leaked metadata rather than removing it; it must not reach learner-facing text.
objections.suggested: ...para indicar uma situação habitual/em andamento, reforçada pelo advérbio いつも ('sempre').

objections.reason: Serialization bug: the whole locale object was stringified into the en slot. `after` value is the literal text `{"en": "使っ is the て form of 使う (促音便: っ gemination before て)", "pt-BR": "使っ é a forma て de 使う (促音便: geminação em っ antes de て)"}` — raw JSON with escaped quotes displayed as a learner note.
objections.suggested: 使っ is the て form of 使う (促音便: っ gemination before て)

objections.reason: gen=false (real Tatoeba pair) yet the patch writes a new English translation, "They're always skipping school.", into a record whose `before` block carries no translation.en at all. The source English of a Layer-A Tatoeba record must not be rewritten by a derived-layer fix; if the stored en really is wrong, that belongs in a note, not in an overwrite. It also introduces a translation.en key that no other record in this batch has, so the shape diverges from the rest of the corpus.
objections.suggested: Leave the Tatoeba source en untouched; drop the added translation.en.

objections.reason: Botched edit left a duplicated tail. `after` reads: "...as emphatic confirmation ('that's right! / exactly!'). そうです is the expression of agreement, not the 〜そうだ of report ('they say that...'), which would require a verb or adjective before it. ('that's right! / exactly!'). そうです is the expression of agreement, not the 〜そうだ of report ('they say that...'), which would require a verb or adjective before it." The entire second half is repeated verbatim, starting mid-parenthetical. Identical duplication in structure_explanation.pt-BR ("...antes. ('é isso mesmo! / exatamente!'). そうです é a expressão de concordância, ... antes.").
objections.suggested: そう (so/that) + です (polite copula 'to be') with an exclamation mark, as emphatic confirmation ('that's right! / exactly!'). そうです is the expression of agreement, not the 〜そうだ of report ('they say that...'), which would require a verb or adjective before it.

objections.reason: The op says the wrong referent appears twice; only the first instance was fixed. `after` still ends "Here ～ものだと expresses an assumed conclusion/supposition ('on the assumption that they were dead')" — the same 彼ら-as-the-dead error the op flagged, now contradicting the corrected "'that (he) was dead'" two clauses earlier. The insertion also breaks the English: "forming 'that (he) was dead'; likewise 'on the assumption that he was dead' and the quotative particle と links..." is ungrammatical and redundant.
objections.suggested: ...死んだ (died/dead) + ものだ forming 'that (he) was dead', and the quotative particle と links this assumption to the verb あきらめた (gave up, past of あきらめる). Here ～ものだと expresses an assumed conclusion/supposition ('on the assumption that he was dead').

objections.reason: The op explicitly states "Both en and pt-BR note texts are wrong", but pt-BR is left untouched at "使っ é a forma て de 使う (sonorização antes de て)". The wrong claim (voicing / 濁音便 instead of 促音便 gemination) still ships in the learner's own language, and it now contradicts the corrected en text (which is itself buried inside the stringified blob).
objections.suggested: 使っ é a forma て de 使う (促音便: geminação em っ antes de て)

objections.reason: The patch edits this exact sentence (prática-se → pratica-se) but leaves the corpus-build metadata inside it: "Como é frase de cobertura, pratica-se número + contador + pergunta com か." This record's own `violations` array flags I5_METADATA_LEAK on both fields, and the batch treats the identical leak in sent:tatoeba-97568 as a major defect — so shipping it here is inconsistent and knowingly leaves a flagged violation in learner text.
objections.suggested: ...e か no fim transforma tudo numa pergunta. (drop the 'Como é frase de cobertura' clause, and the matching 'Since it is a coverage sentence' clause in en)

objections.reason: Half-applied fix. The pt-BR gloss keeps the error the op condemns and now contradicts both its own en counterpart and structure_explanation.pt-BR, which calls やる "o verbo principal".
